page: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v5 is an x86_64 virtual machine tailored for compute tasks requiring moderate memory capacity. It is powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 16 physical cores and 32 threads, yielding 32 dedicated vCPUs managed under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM, representing a 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Processor capabilities include hardware virtualization and vector acceleration via AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic acceleration through AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Storage on the D32ls_v5 is strictly remote, featuring zero local ephemeral disk capacity, and the configuration allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Performance evaluations reflect consistent middle-tier compute capabilities, registering a PassMark CPU score of 36,834.55 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,191.0. Memory subsystem testing places the instance in the upper 25% with a PassMark memory score of 2,756.62 and uncached read bandwidth of 150.05 GB/sec. The instance delivers high throughput in small-model text generation and image processing, but exhibits low performance in large 70B parameter language model inference due to the absence of dedicated GPU acceleration.

Omitting local disk hardware and maintaining a lower memory-to-core ratio allows the D32ls_v5 to optimize infrastructure spend strictly around parallel computing capacity. This hardware composition is well suited for CPU-intensive compilation tasks, automated CI/CD runners, container orchestration workers, stateless web application tiers, and multi-threaded batch operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ls_v5 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 32 vCPUs and 64 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz across 16 physical cores, it supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. The instance operates without local ephemeral storage, routing all persistent I/O through external managed disks, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-core performance coupled with strong memory bandwidth and image processing metrics. Without specialized GPU hardware, large-scale machine learning inference is restricted, though small-model processing remains rapid. The stripped-down storage profile and focused memory allocation make this instance a cost-effective platform for compute-bound batch processing, continuous integration, code compilation, and stateless microservice clusters.
